macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish mixed as Nvidia-led rebound offsets Apple decline
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4%. Nvidia and other technology stocks lifted the market, but Apple declined after warning that higher memory-chip costs could pressure profit margins.

items.title: Fed holds interest rates steady amid persistent inflation concerns
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee reportedly kept its target rate at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, with two members favoring a 25-basis-point increase. Officials upgraded their assessment of economic activity while maintaining concerns about inflationary pressure.

items.title: Markets focus on U.S. midterm results and Middle East uncertainty
items.summary: U.S. equities traded mixed as investors assessed the midterm election outcome and uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict. Canadian officials defended a recent rate increase to 2.5% despite unemployment rising to 5.7%, its highest level since mid-2015.

items.title: AI and semiconductor companies remain central to earnings-driven market volatility
items.summary: Technology shares rebounded after recent losses, while investors continued to assess whether elevated artificial-intelligence valuations are sustainable. AEHR reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $33 million, up 200% year over year, and raised its full-year revenue outlook to $150 million.

items.title: Apple shares fall despite stronger quarterly results
items.summary: Apple reported better-than-expected quarterly results, but its outlook pointed to weaker gross margins as component costs rise. The margin warning weighed on shares and contributed to broader investor concerns about technology-sector earnings.

items.title: Oil prices plunge as Iran peace-talk hopes emerge
items.summary: Crude oil prices fell by more than 7% after comments suggesting there was no rush to restart the Iran war and that Tehran was open to peace talks. Falling energy prices helped shape overnight market sentiment alongside concerns about AI valuations.

items.title: Marvell announces $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum
items.summary: Marvell Technology announced a proposed acquisition of Lumentum valued at $115 billion, adding a major corporate transaction to the recent wave of semiconductor and AI-infrastructure consolidation.

items.title: Oracle plans $20 billion financing for AI infrastructure expansion
items.summary: Oracle announced plans to raise $20 billion through stock and bond offerings to help finance expansion of its artificial-intelligence infrastructure, highlighting the capital intensity of the current AI investment cycle.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $76,000 as crypto market remains under pressure
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $76,900, down about 0.3% over 24 hours, while Ether gained roughly 0.2%, Solana fell 0.5%, and XRP rose 0.4%. Market attention remained focused on U.S. midterm elections, ETF outflows, and fallout from Binance’s security breach.

items.title: Binance reports progress restoring assets after $6.3 billion hack
items.summary: Binance said it had replenished 98% of affected tokens and that roughly $2.85 billion in assets had been frozen or intercepted. The exchange also reported a short-term improvement in capital flows, with approximately $1.6 billion in net inflows over 24 hours.

items.title: Binance hack fallout drives billions in customer withdrawals
items.summary: Customers reportedly withdrew billions of dollars after withdrawals reopened following the breach, while Binance said it had restored or replaced most affected assets. The incident continued to weigh on BNB and broader crypto sentiment.

items.title: Bullish selects Ethereum, Solana and Aptos for stock tokenization
items.summary: Bullish announced that Solana, Aptos, and Ethereum will be the initial blockchain networks for its stock-tokenization service. Solana is expected to be supported first, followed by Aptos and Ethereum, although no launch dates were provided.

items.title: Ethereum researcher targets 2028 post-quantum security transition
items.summary: Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake said leanVM had completed end-to-end formal verification and set December 2028 as a target for Ethereum’s full transition to post-quantum security.

items.title: Megapot to shut down its consumer application
items.summary: On-chain lottery protocol Megapot announced that its megapot.io website and Telegram app will close on December 1. The project said it would shift its focus toward Prizerail, an enterprise-oriented raffle platform.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Bethesda reveals The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel
items.summary: Bethesda announced the subtitle and logo for The Elder Scrolls VI during its 40th-anniversary celebration. The game is associated with Hammerfell, but no release date or platforms were announced.[1][3]

items.title: Xbox reportedly receives bids for Arkane Studios
items.summary: Ubisoft and at least two other companies have reportedly submitted offers for Arkane Studios as Microsoft considers options for the developer. Reports also say Marvel’s Blade may be one to two years from release, though its future could depend on the studio’s ownership.[7]

items.title: Valve slows Steam game review processing
items.summary: Valve said a significant increase in store and page submissions has delayed reviews, with processing times reaching up to 12 business days instead of the typical three to five.[8]

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day adds classic Versus mode
items.summary: The Coalition’s 20th-anniversary update for Gears of War: E-Day brings back a classic Versus mode and adds a limited-time Horde Siege mission, along with anniversary-themed rewards.[9]

items.title: Petit Planet gets December release date
items.summary: HoYoverse announced that the cozy galactic life simulation Petit Planet will launch December 4 on PC, iOS, and Android, with a Nintendo Switch 2 version planned for 2027.[3]

items.title: Borderlands franchise surpasses 100 million units sold
items.summary: The Borderlands series has passed 100 million units sold, with Gearbox continuing to support Borderlands 4 through additional story, bounty, character, raid, and endgame content.[3]
